result.title: Self-Directed Apple Tasting
result.summary: We study the classical apple-tasting setting, a partial feedback model in which the learner observes the true label only when it predicts $1$. A combinatorial characterization for the rates of this problem in the online adversarial setting has been studied by Raman et al. (2024). We study the self-directed setting, in which the learner can adaptively choose the order of the points it predicts on. In the realizable setting, we establish a tetrachotomy on the expected minimax number of mistakes made by any learner. Depending on the VC dimension, the $\emptyset$-centered star number, and the self-directed dimension, we show that the rates could possibly be $Θ(1)$, $O(\log n) \cap ω(1)$, $\tilde Θ(\sqrt{n})$, or $Θ(n)$. In the agnostic setting, the minimax regret is $\tilde Θ(\sqrt{n})$ or $Θ(n)$, depending on the VC dimension.

AI.brief_summary: 研究在线学习中的「apple tasting」部分反馈模型：仅在预测为正时才能看到真实标签；论文分析学习者可自适应选择预测顺序的 self-directed 设定，给出可实现情形下错误数的四分类速率刻画，以及 agnostic 情形的 regret 界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「仅在主动查询时才获得标签、且可自行决定查询顺序」的设定，可能与 LVR 中 LOOK 的证据获取时机与停止决策的理论成本刻画有概念联系，可供核查其自定序与速率结果能否类比推理时的选择性观测。
